clue.text: Outside broadcast abandons filthy row

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so these letters walk out of the longer word

parts.note: filthy means obscene
OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast in television

explanation.surface: A TV crew pulls out of a programme after a sordid quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a noisy public fuss or quarrel, the same as a row.

clue.text: Do the dirty on Ray

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to treat someone unfairly or cheat them, slang verb
second meaning: a beam of light

explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a man's name, but it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shafted is slang for being cheated, and a shaft of light is a single beam.

clue.text: See 9
A great organ on dog, purely for cosmetic purposes

definitions.note: the definition describes the noun by its use: a thing worn purely as make-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: Private Eye is the magazine (an organ) printing the puzzle, so the great organ is the Eye
to dog someone is to follow them closely, to shadow them

explanation.surface: Something huge has been fitted to a dog only to make it look pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine calls itself the Eye, so 'A great organ' is a boast about Private Eye itself; 'on' in a down clue puts it above the word for dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye shadow is coloured make-up on the eyelids, serving no use beyond appearance.

clue.text: Like a bum taking GCE, is wrecked by morphine

parts.note: anal means relating to the anus, the bum

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the British school exam certificate

explanation.surface: A layabout sits an exam while ruined by drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a bum' suggests a tramp, but bum here is the backside; 'wrecked' rearranges GCE and IS into GESIC, and 'taking' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphine is the classic example of a painkilling drug, an analgesic.

clue.text: Agitated state getting vice-president to protect or back his country …

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the first name wraps the other pieces

parts.note: Al Gore was US vice-president at the time, giving his first name AL

indicators.note: back here means going backwards, so the word or is read in reverse

parts.note: Gore's country is the United States, abbreviated USA

explanation.surface: A nation in turmoil calls on the vice-president to defend it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the clue's 'or' round to RO, and 'to protect' has Gore's first name wrap that and his country. The ellipsis links this clue with the next two about Al Gore.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is a state of excitement or stimulation, a stirred-up condition.

clue.text: … the vice-president really tried to get elected — failure…

parts.note: Al Gore, US vice-president, gives AL
so means really, as in 'so good'
to run is to stand for election, past tense ran

explanation.surface: Al Gore campaigned hard for office and lost.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse or candidate that finished unplaced, hence a loser.

clue.text: … stabbed in the back, perhaps, vice-president fashion?

definitions.text: stabbed in the back, perhaps, vice-president fashion?

parts.words: stabbed in the back, perhaps, vice-president fashion?
parts.note: a horn stab is a goring, and the past tense reads as the vice-president's surname with a D on, done in Gore's way

explanation.walkthrough: Gore was the vice-president, so the past tense of being horned looks like his name made into a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gored is being pierced by a horn or tusk, a kind of stabbing.

clue.text: The PM, once demolished Brian Walden-style, er … leaves

indicators.note: a demolished building is knocked down and its parts are rearranged, so the letters are shuffled
when er leaves, those two letters are taken out of the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: Brian Walden was a TV interviewer famous for a 1989 grilling of Margaret Thatcher

explanation.surface: A prime minister was once torn apart by interviewer Brian Walden, who then left hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Walden's famous Thatcher interview; 'leaves' takes E and R out of BRIAN WALDEN STYLE and 'demolished' rearranges what remains into the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin was Conservative Prime Minister three times between the wars.

clue.text: It's Bill's place to present gaily over-the-top Trimble

parts.note: camp means exaggerated and theatrical in a flamboyant way
David Trimble was First Minister of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton's residence is the place to show off David Trimble in flamboyant style.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is Bill Clinton, then US President.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp David is the US President's country retreat in Maryland, so it was Clinton's place.

clue.text: Common lamentable lapse of good sense by top politician?

definitions.text: Common lamentable lapse of good sense by top politician?

parts.words: Common lamentable lapse of good sense by top politician?
parts.note: a stock phrase for a sorry mistake, the kind of words a leader uses when owning up to a blunder

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is what a politician says after a scandal, here aimed at Clinton's confession.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievous error of judgement is a serious misjudgement, the common stock expression for a regrettable blunder.

clue.text: Honest-to goodness male — Brenda's province?

parts.note: honest-to-goodness means genuine, real

explanation.surface: A genuine man is asked whether he is Brenda's area of responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory a monarch rules.

clue.text: Brands carried by no-hope lovers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: burning sticks used as lights
second meaning: someone hopelessly in love is said to carry a torch

explanation.walkthrough: Brands looks like trade names, but it means burning sticks; the idiom 'carry a torch for' gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is an old word for a flaming stick, and unrequited lovers proverbially carry a torch.

clue.text: Acted like a poser, full of holes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: spoke in riddles, as someone who poses puzzles

explanation.walkthrough: A poser looks like a show-off, but it is someone who poses puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle is to set puzzles; riddled also means pierced with many holes.

clue.text: Favoured Field getting out — he doesn't share the orthodox view

definitions.text: he doesn't share the orthodox view

parts.note: in means in favour, popular

indicators.note: getting out suggests breaking loose from order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Frank Field, the Labour MP, taken as written

explanation.surface: A favoured politician named Field quits because he will not follow the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Field left the government in 1998 after his welfare ideas were rejected; 'getting out' rearranges his name to FIDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is an unbeliever, someone rejecting the accepted religion.

clue.text: Socially unacceptable adventurous sailor, not giving head, comes before bench

indicators.note: coming before puts this piece in front of the next
without its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Sinbad is the sailor of the Arabian Nights adventures
a form is a long bench without a back, as in old schools

explanation.surface: A rude sailor, refusing oral sex, is brought up before the magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: In bad form is an idiom for bad manners, behaviour not acceptable in polite company.

clue.text: Dancer makes arse-over-tip dash to get our mag, before five

indicators.note: before puts the magazine ahead of the next piece
head over heels, turned upside down, so in an across clue the word is read backwards

parts.note: to dash is to run
Private Eye is the magazine printing the puzzle
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A dancer tumbles while hurrying to buy Private Eye before five o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was the celebrated Russian ballet star.

clue.text: The president stuffing First Lady and Lewinsky (head only) in hen-house

indicators.note: stuffing means filling something, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: a roost is where hens perch
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: only the head of the word, its first letter

parts.note: Monica Lewinsky, whose affair with Clinton was the scandal of 1998

explanation.surface: The president beds his wife and Lewinsky in a hen-house.
explanation.walkthrough: First Lady suggests the president's wife; it is Eve, the first woman. 'head only' keeps the first letter of Lewinsky, and 'stuffing' puts both inside the hen-house word.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin and Theodore Roosevelt were both US presidents.

clue.text: See 7
Incapable of getting member reduced in size

definitions.note: incapable is British slang for helplessly drunk, as is the answer

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
less means smaller, reduced in amount

explanation.surface: Someone can't get a body part shrunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for so drunk one cannot stand, drunk and incapable.

clue.text: Soundly understands business of hooter operation

indicators.note: said soundly, the word is heard spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: to know is to understand
a job is a piece of business, a task

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly grasps the trade of cosmetic surgery on noses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'sensibly' but says the word for understands is heard, not spelt. A hooter is British slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose job is a cosmetic rhinoplasty, surgery reshaping the nose.

clue.text: Took the piss — got well stuffed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mocked, jeered, British slang
second meaning: ate greedily, wolfed food

explanation.walkthrough: To take the piss is British slang for mockery; to scoff is both to jeer and to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoffing means mocking with contempt, and in British slang also eating food quickly.

clue.text: Support rock band in the pen

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the enclosure

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock group plays inside a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock band' looks like a music group, but rock is the anagram signal, making ANDB, and 'in' sets that inside the word for a pig pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A standby is a backup, someone or something kept ready to support.

clue.text: Far out politician embraces EU — it's a conspiracy!

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged
to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the politician's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written: the European Union

explanation.surface: A far-out politician backing Europe is accused of plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far out' reads as hippy slang for amazing, but 'out' rearranges Far to FRA, and 'embraces' has the politician hug the EU letters, giving MEUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame-up is a plot to make an innocent person appear guilty.

clue.text: Stupid gits Ed's organised to produce news summaries

indicators.note: organised means arranged into order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Stupid idiots on the editor's staff put together the news round-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Stupid looks like the anagram signal but is surface only; organised does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary of news or writing.

clue.text: Nick, we hear, the old party leader

indicators.note: we hear means spoken aloud, the word heard rather than written

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick, reportedly, once led the party.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a name; it is slang for stealing, and 'we hear' says the answer only sounds like that word.
explanation.definitionFit: David Steel was the last leader of the Liberal Party before its 1988 merger.

clue.text: Mean woman stuck inside a long time

indicators.note: stuck inside means placed within, so the name goes into the other piece

parts.note: an age is a very long time
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A stingy woman has been shut indoors for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean looks like stingy; it is the arithmetic mean. 'stuck inside' puts the woman within the long time.
explanation.definitionFit: The average is the mean value of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Put down Carpenters' piece

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a run of letters taken from inside it

parts.note: the name of the pop duo, the Carpenters, holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Someone records an item by the Carpenters, the 1970s pop duo.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carpenters were Karen and Richard Carpenter's pop act; 'piece' says to take a stretch of letters from inside their name, which gives the word in carpENTERs.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something in a ledger or diary is to put it down in writing.

clue.text: Well-rounded in bathrobe (see-through)

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of bathrobe and the start of see-through

explanation.surface: A curvy figure is visible in a sheer bathrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: Well-rounded looks like a compliment on character; it means fat. 'in' says the letters lie within the words, running across bathrobe and see.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very fat, so a round figure in the literal sense.

clue.text: See 9
Many constituents petitioning their MP, a deserting pisspoor abysmal s.o.b.

indicators.note: pisspoor is slang for very bad, so the letters are a mess and rearranged
a deserting means the letter a leaves the pool before the shuffle

parts.note: the letters of these words, s.o.b. taken without its dots

explanation.surface: Voters lobbying their MP call him an abysmal son of a bitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a deserting' takes A out of ABYSMAL SOB, and 'pisspoor', slang for dreadful, rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass lobby is a large crowd of constituents going together to press MPs.

clue.text: Drunk giving head to Brenda

parts.note: the top is the head of something
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, ER

explanation.surface: A drunk performs a sexual act on the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Drunk looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a habitual heavy drinker, an old word for a drunkard.
